title: MyLibrary
summary: A library management system built with Flask and PostgreSQL — my Diploma minor project.
description: MyLibrary is my minor academic project — a full library management system that digitises the day-to-day operations of a small library.
It handles book cataloguing, member records, and borrow/return tracking, with a clean web interface on top of a relational database.
problem: Small libraries still rely on registers and spreadsheets, making it hard to track which books are out, overdue, or reserved.
whyBuilt: Built as my Diploma minor project to apply backend fundamentals end to end — from schema design to a working web app.
whatLearned: Relational schema design, Flask routing and templating, session-based authentication, and deployment basics.

title: venue-navigator (Setu)
summary: AI stadium concierge for FIFA World Cup 2026 — deterministic Dijkstra routing with Gemini explanations.
description: venue-navigator is an AI stadium concierge built for the FIFA World Cup 2026 experience. Fans can plan how to reach their seat, find amenities, and get plain-language explanations of the best route.
Routing is deliberately deterministic — computed with Dijkstra's algorithm, never LLM-routed — while Gemini is used only to turn the computed path into a friendly, conversational explanation.
The app is a React 18 / TypeScript PWA with 153 tests, built to stay reliable and offline-friendly on match day.
problem: Large stadiums are confusing: fans waste time finding gates, seats, and amenities, and AI navigation tools are often unreliable because the LLM does the routing.
whyBuilt: Built to prove that you can get the best of both worlds — trustworthy algorithmic routing plus a helpful AI interface — in a high-stakes, high-scale setting.
whatLearned: Graph-based shortest-path routing, PWA patterns, React 18 with TypeScript, and a test discipline that keeps 153 tests meaningful.

title: ecotrace (EcoTrace)
summary: Carbon-footprint awareness platform with India-specific emission factors.
description: EcoTrace is a carbon-footprint awareness platform that estimates the emissions behind everyday choices using India-specific factors rather than global averages.
The front end is a React 19 app talking to an Express + Gemini backend, deployed on Cloud Run, with the Gemini layer used to explain results in plain language.
problem: Most carbon calculators use generic global factors, so estimates for Indian households are inaccurate and unrelatable.
whyBuilt: To make sustainability data relevant to Indian users and to practice a full React + Express + cloud deployment stack.
whatLearned: React 19 and Express app structure, working with LLM APIs for explanations, and deploying to Cloud Run.

title: Votermitra-Ai (VoterMitra AI)
summary: Bilingual civic-education assistant for Indian elections, built on Google Cloud.
description: VoterMitra AI is a bilingual civic-education assistant that helps Indian voters understand elections — how to register, where to vote, and what's on the ballot.

It is a Next.js app that combines Gemini for natural-language answers with Firestore for content, Google Maps for locating polling stations, and a Calendar integration for election-day reminders — all running on GCP.
problem: Election information is scattered, and non-English speakers face an even higher barrier to understanding the voting process.
whyBuilt: To put civic information in the hands of every Indian voter in their own language, and to ship a real multi-service Google Cloud application.
whatLearned: Next.js full-stack structure, integrating Gemini, Firestore, Maps and Calendar, and deploying multi-service apps on GCP.

title: Smart-Stadium-Flow-System-SSF (StadiumPulse Pro)
summary: Stadium crowd-intelligence and safety dashboard with predictive velocity modelling.
description: StadiumPulse Pro is a crowd-intelligence dashboard that helps venue operators understand and predict how crowds move inside a stadium.
It is built with vanilla JavaScript on the front end and an Express backend, with predictive velocity modelling to anticipate congestion, and GCP observability throughout.
problem: Crowd surges are hard to predict in real time, and operators lack a single view of how movement patterns evolve during an event.
whyBuilt: To explore predictive modelling applied to real-world safety, with a focus on clear visualisation and cloud observability.
whatLearned: Predictive modelling of movement data, event-driven dashboards with vanilla JS, and GCP observability tooling.

title: CyberGuard-NIDS
description: CyberGuard-NIDS is a network intrusion detection dashboard built with a Random Forest model and a Streamlit interface.
It was built during the EDUNET Cybersecurity with Generative AI internship, taking the intrusion-detection concepts from the curriculum and turning them into a working tool.
problem: Traditional signature-based intrusion detection misses novel attacks; ML-based detection needs a usable way to inspect and interpret results.
whyBuilt: Built as the hands-on deliverable of the EDUNET internship to apply ML to real security problems.
whatLearned: Random Forest classification, feature handling for network traffic, and building an interactive dashboard with Streamlit.

title: TypeTrace
summary: Educational keystroke-logging simulator (Tkinter) that demonstrates cybersecurity risks.
description: TypeTrace is an educational simulator written with Python's Tkinter that shows how keystroke loggers work and why they are dangerous.
It is a safe, sandboxed demonstration built to teach others the mechanics behind keylogging attacks — for learning, not for real-world use.
problem: Most people don't understand how keystroke loggers operate, which makes them easier to fall victim to.
whyBuilt: To turn the social-engineering and toolkit concepts from the EDUNET internship into a hands-on teaching tool.
whatLearned: Tkinter UI development, event handling, and communicating security concepts through demos.

title: PyTasks
summary: CLI task manager with persistent JSON storage.
description: PyTasks is a command-line task manager that keeps your to-dos in persistent JSON storage, so nothing is lost between sessions.
It is a focused exercise in clean CLI design, file I/O, and data persistence in plain Python.
problem: Simple to-do lists are scattered across apps or notes, and terminal users want something lightweight and scriptable.
whyBuilt: A self-directed project to practise Python CLI structure and durable storage without a database dependency.
whatLearned: CLI argument handling, JSON persistence, and structuring a small tool with clear user flows.
